T1.implementation_approach: Design a user-friendly interface for browsing, searching, and filtering problems using wireframes and mockups.

T2.implementation_approach: Develop backend APIs to handle problem data retrieval, creation, and updates using a framework like Node.js or Django.

T3.implementation_approach: Set up a relational database schema to store problem details, tags, and metadata.
T3.notes: Use a database like PostgreSQL or MySQL.

T4.implementation_approach: Design an intuitive UI for users to submit code, view results, and track submission history.
T4.notes: Include real-time feedback for code execution.

T5.implementation_approach: Implement backend logic to handle code submissions, execute code securely, and return results.
T5.notes: Use containerization tools like Docker for secure code execution.

T6.implementation_approach: Set up a database to store code submissions, execution results, and timestamps.
T6.notes: Ensure proper indexing for efficient retrieval.

T7.implementation_approach: Create a UI for users to view and edit their profiles, including personal details and activity history.
T7.notes: Focus on personalization and ease of use.

T8.implementation_approach: Develop backend APIs to manage user profile data, authentication, and authorization.
T8.notes: Implement secure password storage and validation.

T9.implementation_approach: Set up a database schema to store user information, preferences, and activity logs.
T9.notes: Ensure data privacy and compliance with regulations.

T10.implementation_approach: Design a visually appealing leaderboard UI to display top users based on various metrics.

T11.implementation_approach: Implement backend logic to calculate and retrieve leaderboard data dynamically.

T12.implementation_approach: Set up a database to store leaderboard metrics and user rankings.
T12.notes: Ensure efficient querying for large datasets.

T13.implementation_approach: Develop a UI for tutorials and hints, including navigation and interactive elements.
T13.notes: Ensure content is easy to access and visually engaging.

T14.implementation_approach: Implement backend APIs to serve tutorial and hint content dynamically.

T15.implementation_approach: Set up a database to store tutorial and hint content, including metadata and versioning.
T15.notes: Ensure scalability for future content additions.

T16.implementation_approach: Perform thorough testing of all frontend components for functionality, responsiveness, and usability.
T16.notes: Use tools like Selenium or Cypress.

T17.implementation_approach: Test backend APIs for performance, security, and correctness using tools like Postman or JMeter.

T18.implementation_approach: Validate database schema, queries, and data integrity through automated and manual testing.
T18.notes: Focus on data consistency and performance.

T19.implementation_approach: Deploy the application using cloud services like AWS or Azure, ensuring proper CI/CD pipelines.

from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

# Initialize the SQLAlchemy object
db = SQLAlchemy()

from app.database import db

class Problem(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'problems'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    difficulty = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.now())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Problem {self.id} - {self.title}>"

    def to_dict(self):
        return {
            "id": self.id,
            "title": self.title,
            "description": self.description,
            "difficulty": self.difficulty,
            "created_at": self.created_at,
            "updated_at": self.updated_at
        }

from app.database import db
from datetime import datetime

class User(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'users'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    username = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False, unique=True)
    email = db.Column(db.String(120), nullable=False, unique=True)
    password_hash = db.Column(db.String(128), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow)
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow, onupdate=datetime.utcnow)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<User {self.username}>"

    def to_dict(self):
        return {
            "id": self.id,
            "username": self.username,
            "email": self.email,
            "created_at": self.created_at.isoformat(),
            "updated_at": self.updated_at.isoformat(),
        }

from app.database import db
from app.models.user import User
from app.models.problem import Problem
from datetime import datetime

class Solution(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'solutions'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    user_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('users.id'), nullable=False)
    problem_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('problems.id'), nullable=False)
    code = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    language = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    submitted_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow, nullable=False)
    is_correct = db.Column(db.Boolean, default=False, nullable=False)

    user = db.relationship('User', backref='solutions', lazy=True)
    problem = db.relationship('Problem', backref='solutions', lazy=True)

    def to_dict(self):
        return {
            'id': self.id,
            'user_id': self.user_id,
            'problem_id': self.problem_id,
            'code': self.code,
            'language': self.language,
            'submitted_at': self.submitted_at.isoformat() if self.submitted_at else None,
            'is_correct': self.is_correct
        }

from flask import Blueprint, request, jsonify
from app.database import db
from app.models.solution import Solution
from app.models.problem import Problem
from app.models.user import User

solution_bp = Blueprint('solution', __name__)

# Endpoint to list all solutions
@solution_bp.route('/solutions/', methods=['GET'])
def list_solutions():
    solutions = Solution.query.all()
    return jsonify([solution.to_dict() for solution in solutions]), 200

# Endpoint to view a specific solution
@solution_bp.route('/solutions/<int:solution_id>', methods=['GET'])
def view_solution(solution_id):
    solution = Solution.query.get(solution_id)
    if not solution:
        return jsonify({'error': 'Solution not found'}), 404
    return jsonify(solution.to_dict()), 200

# Endpoint to create a new solution
@solution_bp.route('/solutions/create', methods=['POST'])
def create_solution():
    data = request.get_json()
    if not data or 'problem_id' not in data or 'user_id' not in data or 'content' not in data:
        return jsonify({'error': 'Invalid input'}), 400

    problem = Problem.query.get(data['problem_id'])
    user = User.query.get(data['user_id'])
    if not problem or not user:
        return jsonify({'error': 'Problem or User not found'}), 404

    new_solution = Solution(
        problem_id=data['problem_id'],
        user_id=data['user_id'],
        content=data['content']
    )
    db.session.add(new_solution)
    db.session.commit()

    return jsonify(new_solution.to_dict()), 201

# Endpoint to edit an existing solution
@solution_bp.route('/solutions/<int:solution_id>/edit', methods=['PUT'])
def edit_solution(solution_id):
    solution = Solution.query.get(solution_id)
    if not solution:
        return jsonify({'error': 'Solution not found'}), 404

    data = request.get_json()
    if not data:
        return jsonify({'error': 'Invalid input'}), 400

    solution.content = data.get('content', solution.content)
    db.session.commit()

    return jsonify(solution.to_dict()), 200

# Endpoint to delete a solution
@solution_bp.route('/solutions/<int:solution_id>/delete', methods=['DELETE'])
def delete_solution(solution_id):
    solution = Solution.query.get(solution_id)
    if not solution:
        return jsonify({'error': 'Solution not found'}), 404

    db.session.delete(solution)
    db.session.commit()

    return jsonify({'message': 'Solution deleted successfully'}), 200

# app/routes.py
from flask import Flask
from app.controllers.problem_controller import problem_bp
from app.controllers.user_controller import user_bp
from app.controllers.solution_controller import solution_bp

def register_routes(app: Flask):
    """
    Register all blueprints with the Flask application.
    """
    app.register_blueprint(problem_bp)
    app.register_blueprint(user_bp)
    app.register_blueprint(solution_bp)

from flask import Flask, render_template
from app.database import db
from app.routes import register_routes

def create_app():
    # Initialize the Flask application
    app = Flask(
        __name__,
        template_folder='../templates',
        static_folder='../static',
        static_url_path='/static'
    )

    # Configure the app (add database configurations here if needed)
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI'] = 'sqlite:///app.db'  # Example: Replace with your database URI
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_TRACK_MODIFICATIONS'] = False

    # Initialize the database
    db.init_app(app)

    # Register routes (blueprints)
    register_routes(app)

    # Define the home route
    @app.route('/')
    def home():
        return render_template('index.html')

    return app

code_repository.readme_content:
# ACM Problem-Solving Platform

A website designed to help users solve ACM programming problems efficiently.

## Features

- Problem Repository: A comprehensive collection of ACM programming problems categorized by difficulty and topic.
- Code Submission System: Allows users to submit their code and receive instant feedback on correctness and performance.
- User Profiles: Enables users to create profiles to track their progress and achievements.
- Leaderboard: Displays rankings based on user performance and problem-solving activity.
- Tutorials and Hints: Provides educational resources and hints to help users understand and solve problems.

## Setup

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python app.py
```

## Usage

Open http://localhost:5000 in your browser.
